brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource Team: How to Activate a New Accounting Firm

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the License Service in the ESource system?
choices: To store client names, bank statements, and transactions securely
To send sign-in codes, enforce plan limits, keep book counts, and issue access keys
To manage the firm's logo and branding colors
To process monthly billing payments from firms
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the License Service handles authentication, plan enforcement, and book counting without ever seeing sensitive client data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The License Service is designed specifically for security and access control. It intentionally does not receive client names, bank statements, or transactions, keeping sensitive data on the firm's own computers.

questions.question: What should you collect from a firm before activation?
choices: Only the firm's legal name and web address
The firm's legal name, logo file, brand color, web address, and owner's name and work email
The firm's tier, plan limits, and the pricing agreement
A signed agreement and the firm's security lead contact information
questions.feedback_correct: You've got it—those specific details are needed to set up the firm's profile and get the owner ready to sign in.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While some of those items are part of the activation checklist, the instructor notes specifically list the firm's details you need to collect: legal name, logo file, brand color, web address, and owner's name and work email.

questions.question: What is a Firm ID and what are its key characteristics?
choices: The firm's legal name, which can include spaces and capital letters
A short, lowercase identifier with no spaces that never changes once chosen
The firm's web address, such as smithco.esourcebookkeeper.com
The owner's email address used to sign in to the admin page
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the Firm ID is a permanent identifier, so it needs to be chosen carefully and follows strict formatting rules.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Firm ID is a specific internal identifier, not the firm's legal name or web address. It's short, lowercase, has no spaces, and is permanent, so it requires careful selection.

questions.question: In the profiles.js file, what does the 'firm' setting control?
choices: The firm's web address and domain configuration
The name clients see on statement requests and Excel reports
The storage location where the firm's books are saved
The tier and book limit displayed on the admin page
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—the 'firm' setting determines how the firm appears to clients on reports and statements.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While 'name' shows at the top of the screen for staff, the 'firm' setting is specifically what clients see on statement requests and every sheet of the Excel reports.

questions.question: When setting up a domain in Vercel and Cloudflare, why is it important to set the proxy cloud to gray instead of orange?
choices: Gray cloud is faster and reduces latency for the firm's users
Orange cloud prevents the firm from branding its profile correctly
Gray (DNS only) allows Vercel's security certificate to work; orange cloud blocks it
Gray cloud is required by the License Service to issue access keys
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this is a critical security step; the orange cloud would interfere with Vercel's SSL certificate.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The cloud color in Cloudflare controls how traffic is routed. Gray means DNS only, which allows Vercel's security certificate to function properly. An orange cloud would block that certificate.

questions.question: How long does a sign-in code remain valid when the owner first tries to access the firm?
choices: Five minutes
Ten minutes
Twenty minutes
One hour
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the six-digit code sent by email is only good for ten minutes, so the owner needs to act quickly.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sign-in code is time-sensitive to protect security. According to the course, it works for ten minutes from when it is sent.

questions.question: What does the help assistant in the firm's profile do, and what information does it have access to?
choices: It answers how-to questions only and never sees client books
It provides technical support for Vercel and Cloudflare configuration
It processes billing and calculates monthly book counts
It manages the License Service and enforces plan limits
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the assistant is designed for user support only and is intentionally kept separate from sensitive client data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The help assistant is a limited feature focused on answering how-to questions. It is deliberately isolated from client books to maintain security and privacy.

questions.question: How is a firm billed each month, and what specific metric determines the amount owed?
choices: The total number of books ever added to the firm's account
The highest number of active client books on any single day that month
A flat fee per staff member plus a per-book rate
The average number of books used throughout the month divided by the number of days
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—billing is based on peak usage in a month, not total or average, which makes the counting straightforward.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The License Service tracks the highest number of active books across any single day in the month. This peak-usage model is simpler and fairer than averaging or counting total books ever added.

questions.question: A firm's employee leaves the company—what steps must be taken to secure their access, and what happens to their offline books?
choices: The owner removes them from the License tab; their computer locks at the next check-in and books remain encrypted
The employee's access is removed by the admin page; all their books are immediately deleted
The firm must contact ESource support to revoke access; offline books are transferred to another user
The owner removes them from the License tab, but books remain accessible until the employee's laptop connects to the internet
questions.feedback_correct: That's the right security procedure—the owner uses the License tab for access control, and the encryption on the laptop keeps data safe.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When an employee leaves, the firm's owner removes them from the License tab. The books on their computer stay encrypted and secure, and the device locks when it next checks in with the License Service.

questions.question: Based on the activation checklist at the end of the course, why is it important to verify the signed agreement before any other activation steps?
choices: The agreement contains the Firm ID that must be used on the admin page
It confirms the firm's tier and book limit are legally binding and establishes the terms you will use for billing
It provides the web address and logo that will be used in Vercel configuration
It includes the owner's sign-in credentials and the initial staff member list
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the agreement is foundational because it locks in the tier, limits, and billing terms before you proceed with technical setup.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The signed agreement is the first item on the activation checklist because it establishes the legal and financial terms (tier and book limit) that will guide the rest of the setup and determine monthly billing.
